universities.name: Indian Institute of Information Technology Tiruchirappalli
universities.summary: IIIT Tiruchirappalli is a not-for-profit public-private-partnership institute at Sethurapatti in Tamil Nadu, started in 2013 and an Institute of National Importance under the IIIT (Public-Private Partnership) Act, 2017. It offers B.Tech. programmes in computing and electronics, M.Tech. programmes and doctoral research.
universities.campusLifestyle: The institute has worked from its permanent Sethurapatti campus on the Trichy-Madurai highway since June 2021. Its hostel page lists a residence hall, a mess hall and a gym. Before that it ran from temporary premises at NIT Tiruchirappalli from 2016 and at Oxford Engineering College from 2020, so older references to those addresses are out of date.
universities.cityProfile: The permanent campus is at Sethurapatti on the Tiruchirappalli-Madurai highway, Tamil Nadu 620012. The institute's 2026 reporting guide puts it about 20 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction and the Central bus stand, with buses to most of Tamil Nadu, southern Karnataka and Kerala.
universities.practicalExposure: IIIT Tiruchirappalli describes an agreement with SVNIT Surat covering joint research, academic activities and innovation, with internship opportunities for B.Tech. and M.Tech. students among its stated scope. These are opportunities within the collaboration, not a guarantee of an internship or placement. Industry partners named by the institute are TCS, Cognizant, Infosys, Ramco Systems, ELCOT and Navitas.
universities.hostelOverview: First-semester hostel payments for 2026-27 are INR 45,600: hostel admission fee INR 1,200, establishment charges INR 7,200, licence, electricity and water INR 13,200 and a mess advance of INR 24,000. A refundable hostel deposit of INR 4,800 is charged once. Rooms are allotted by the warden, and residents sign in and out; the 2024-25 rules prohibit cooking and heaters, kettles and air conditioners in rooms.
universities.dietarySupport: The mess serves breakfast 7:00 to 9:00 am, lunch noon to 2:00 pm, snacks 4:45 to 6:00 pm and dinner 7:00 to 9:00 pm, under the 2024-25 hostel rules, which allow no relaxation of timings. Complaints go to the warden. The institute publishes no menu or provision for specific regional, religious or medical diets.
universities.safetyOverview: The hostel rules treat ragging as a cognizable offence and encourage residents to report it immediately; admitted students also file an anti-ragging declaration. Boys' hostel residents must be back by 10:00 pm, visitors sign the book at the entrance, and emergency contact numbers are given at room allotment.
universities.studentSupport: The admissions pages give reporting instructions, a hostel accommodation form and a cancellation form, and link to the National Scholarship Portal notice for 2026-27. Admission does not guarantee a scholarship. Students Traffic counselling can help you compare routes and prepare documents.
whyChoose: A focused B.Tech. portfolio in computer science, AI and data science, and electronics with VLSI, taught at a statutory Institute of National Importance.
DASA seats are set aside for foreign nationals, OCI/PIO candidates, NRIs and CIWG children, with published tuition by category.
A permanent campus about 20 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction, with hostel and mess charges published.
thingsToConsider: DASA admission needs a valid JEE (Main) score, 75 per cent in Class 12 and, for Indian nationals and OCI/PIO(I), two years of schooling abroad.
The DASA matrix offers only 6 to 9 Non-CIWG and 2 to 5 CIWG seats per branch, so places are few.
Published fees are for the first semester only and exclude a further INR 92,000 of other charges, so they are not annual tuition.
bestFitFor: NRIs, OCI/PIO candidates and foreign nationals with a JEE (Main) score who want a computing or electronics B.Tech. in Tamil Nadu.
Children of Indian workers in the Gulf who qualify for CIWG seats and can document a parent's employment.
Students comfortable with a residential campus outside the city centre.

faq.question: Is IIIT Tiruchirappalli a government institute?
faq.answer: It is a not-for-profit public-private-partnership institute funded by the Government of India, the Tamil Nadu government and industry partners in a 50:35:15 ratio. The IIIT (Public-Private Partnership) Act, 2017 lists it in its Schedule and declares it an institution of national importance.

faq.question: Where is the IIIT Tiruchirappalli campus?
faq.answer: At Sethurapatti on the Trichy-Madurai highway, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu 620012, about 20 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction. The institute moved there in June 2021 from earlier temporary premises.

faq.question: Which B.Tech. programmes does IIIT Tiruchirappalli offer?
faq.answer: Four, each of four years: Computer Science and Engineering; CSE (Artificial Intelligence and Data Science); Electronics and Communication Engineering; and ECE (VLSI Design). All four have DASA 2026 seats.

faq.question: Can international students join IIIT Tiruchirappalli?
faq.answer: Foreign nationals, OCI/PIO candidates and NRIs can enter the B.Tech. through DASA with a valid JEE (Main) score and 75 per cent in Class 12. Indian nationals and OCI/PIO(I) candidates also need two years of schooling abroad.

faq.question: How many DASA seats does IIIT Tiruchirappalli have?
faq.answer: The 2026 matrix lists 9 Non-CIWG and 5 CIWG seats each in CSE and CSE (AI and DS), and 6 Non-CIWG seats each in ECE and ECE (VLSI Design), with 3 and 2 CIWG seats respectively. Seat numbers change each cycle.

faq.question: What are the DASA tuition fees at IIIT Tiruchirappalli?
faq.answer: For the 2026-27 first semester, tuition was USD 4,000 for Non-SAARC and USD 2,000 for SAARC students, and INR 1,15,200 for CIWG students. A further INR 92,000 covered one-time, institute, hostel and mess charges.

faq.question: Are the published B.Tech. fees annual?
faq.answer: No. The fee sheet is for the first, odd semester of 2026-27 and includes refundable deposits, so it should not be doubled to estimate a year.

faq.question: What documents are needed to report for the DASA B.Tech.?
faq.answer: Class 10, 11 and 12 mark sheets, the DASA school certificate, passport, JEE (Main) cards, the DASA admission letter, a medical certificate and, for NRI or OCI/PIO(I) candidates, proof of two years of schooling abroad. CIWG candidates add parent employment documents.

faq.question: Does IIIT Tiruchirappalli have hostels?
faq.answer: Yes, a residence hall and mess hall are listed. First-semester hostel charges for 2026-27 were INR 45,600 including a INR 24,000 mess advance, plus a refundable INR 4,800 deposit. Room allotment is by the warden.

faq.question: Is the teaching language confirmed?
faq.answer: The programme pages checked do not state it. Ask the department about lectures, assessment and any language requirement before accepting an offer.
